newsitem.title: USA: USDA lowers ag export forecast for FY 1996.
newsitem.headline: USDA lowers ag export forecast for FY 1996.

text.p: The U.S. Agriculture Department Friday revised down its estimate for U.S. agricultural exports in fiscal year 1996 to $59.8 billion from $60 billion previously seen due to a sluggish September.

In its monthly Agricultural Trade Update, USDA said the revised export estimate still set a record and was up 10 percent from $54.2 billion in fiscal year 1995. U.S. exports for fiscal year 1997 are pegged at $58 billion.
USDA said September exports were $4.4 billion, down seven percent from September 1995. Poor corn sales took a bite out of the monthly total.

USDA said September corn exports were 2.5 million tonnes, down 60 percent from a year earlier and that volume for the year fell 10 percent from fiscal 1995 to 52.7 million tonnes. Notably, September corn exports to Japan fell 32 percent from a year earlier. Japan was the leading market for U.S. corn in 1996, taking 14.9 million tonnes, USDA noted.
U.S wheat and soybean exports also dipped in September.

On wheat, USDA said in its trade update that exports fell three percent in September to 3.4 million tonnes from a year earlier. Looking at the entire year, USDA noted Egpyt was the leading market for U.S. wheat in fiscal 1996, buying 5.4 million tonnes. Exports to China fell by 39 percent for the year, ending at 2.3 million tonnes, it said.
Soybean exports were 1.1 million tonnes in September, off 793,000 tonnes from September 1995, USDA said. The European Union and Japan were the leading markets that month, it added.
